content:
Certainly! This passage is from **Homer's Iliad, Book 19 (lines 182–200)**. Here is an accurate, context-conscious translation into English:

---

But then the lord of men, Agamemnon, answered him:

"Son of Laertes, I am glad to hear your words;
For you have set all things out and spoken in due measure.
And I myself am willing to swear an oath, as my heart bids me,
Nor shall I swear falsely by the god. But Achilles
should remain here, eager though he is for war;
And all the others stay assembled here together,
until the gifts are brought forth from my hut,
and we make solemn oaths of faith.
You yourself, I charge and command,
choose out the best youths of all the Achaeans;
to bring the gifts from my tent, all that we promised yesterday to give Achilles,
and the women too.
And let Talthybius quickly across the wide army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar for sacrifice to Zeus and to the Sun."
